extracted.intended_audience: Members of the American Mathematical Society; mathematicians considering AMS governance and elections
extracted.subtask_description: Biographical sketches and short position statements from candidates for AMS offices describing what the Society and its Council/Trustees should do; useful as a set of policy/quality criteria for AMS governance, outreach, and support of the profession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate teaching and research communities
rubrics_metrics.description: (original phrasing) "Integrating the teaching community with the research community."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates propose fostering closer ties between college/school teachers and research mathematicians; examples given include programs to bring college teachers into the university for updating (PEW, DANA) and NSF/Mathematics Teacher programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and draw in mathematically talented minorities and women
rubrics_metrics.description: (original phrasing) "Identifying the mathematically talented among minority groups and women, drawing them into our community."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit emphasis on outreach and recruitment targeted at underrepresented groups; candidates mention cooperative research programs with minority institutions and active promotion of women/minority candidates for AMS offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise leadership in undergraduate education excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: (original phrasing) "I believe that AMS should exercise leadership in the commitment of the research mathematics community to excellence in undergraduate education."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call for AMS to lead improvements in undergraduate teaching quality, including supporting programs (e.g., summer institutes, special projects), and to couple this with graduate support to attract careers in mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take active role in improvement of mathematics teaching at all levels
rubrics_metrics.description: (original phrasing) "take an active role in the improvement of mathematics teaching at all levels"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed actions include supporting curricular reform, faculty updating programs, teacher development projects, and communicating importance of such efforts to funding bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize importance of mathematics (especially basic/undirected research) to funders and public
rubrics_metrics.description: (original phrasing) "emphasize to funding sources and to the general public the importance of mathematics especially the kind of undirected basic research carried out by individual investigators."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocacy role: inform government and public of value of basic mathematical research to secure and protect funding; use AMS communications and outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitate interdisciplinary interaction within mathematics and with other fields
rubrics_metrics.description: (original phrasing) "facilitate interdisciplinary interaction both within mathematics and between mathematics and other fields."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support programs and conferences encouraging cross-disciplinary work (e.g., math/physics/biology), and strengthen institutional links and collaborative funding opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage talented students (including women/minorities) to pursue mathematics careers
rubrics_metrics.description: (original phrasing) "strongly encourage talented students, including women and members of minority groups, to consider mathematics as a career."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recruitment and retention strategies such as freshman programs to hold students in mathematics, targeted outreach, mentoring, and visibility of role models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a forum to discuss relations between mathematics and society
rubrics_metrics.description: (original phrasing) "provide a forum for mathematicians to discuss the relations between mathematics and society."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize meetings, panels, and publications addressing public policy, education, and the societal impact of mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address the job shortage and research funding crisis
rubrics_metrics.description: (original phrasing) "The two most severe crises ... are the shortage of jobs and the difficulty of obtaining research funding."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council should actively seek methods to deal with job market problems and funding shortages, including task forces, advocacy with agencies, and exploring new funding sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council openness and accountability to membership
rubrics_metrics.description: (original phrasing) "I would also like the AMS council to function more openly and to be more accountable to the AMS membership at large."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Governance reforms to increase transparency, member communication, and accountability in Council decisions and priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set up a task force to project and assess the future job market
rubrics_metrics.description: (original phrasing) "It should be the responsibility of the American Mathematical Society to set up a task force to effectively deal with this problem [project and accurately assess the future market]."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form a dedicated panel to analyze employment trends and recommend policies to improve hiring prospects for students and early-career mathematicians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confront the flow of students away from mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: (original phrasing) "the Council needs to have frank discussions about practical ways to stem the flow of American college and graduate students away from mathematics and the sciences."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy actions aimed at education reform, funding, career incentives, and public messaging to retain student interest in mathematical careers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider effects of policy changes on research support (e.g., salary cap removal)
rubrics_metrics.description: (original phrasing) "a close look ought to be taken at the effect on NSF grants of the removal of the salary cap."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how external policy decisions (federal salary caps, agency rules) influence grant distribution and investigator support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Represent and support faculty at small colleges and less-resourced institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: (original phrasing) "A substantial proportion of AMS members are faculty at small colleges and universities ... This segment of the membership has little representation on the AMS Council, and it is sometimes overlooked."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure Council and Society programs include and address needs of mathematicians at small institutions (teaching support, representation, tailored funding/training).

rubrics_metrics.name: Convince public that mathematics is not produced by a few for many
rubrics_metrics.description: (original phrasing) "we must convince the public that mathematics is not a product which can be manufactured by a few to be consumed by many; that knowledge and discovery go hand in hand at all levels of mathematics."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public education and outreach emphasizing distributed creativity in mathematics and importance of supporting broad participation at all levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trustee duty to address profession-wide issues responsibly
rubrics_metrics.description: (original phrasing) "It is incumbent upon a Trustee to see that issues of our profession are seriously attended to such as: scarcity of jobs, educational reform, inequities due to race and sex, government support of research, and careful use of Society funds."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trustees should prioritize these topics in oversight and resource allocation; ensure Society funds are used to address job, education, equity, and funding challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain high standards while avoiding elitism
rubrics_metrics.description: (original phrasing) "High standards should be maintained while avoiding elitism. All qualified and interested individuals should be encouraged to pursue careers in mathematics and to advance their careers as far as possible."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance excellence with inclusivity: uphold rigorous scholarship but implement measures (mentoring, outreach, affirmative action) to broaden participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocate affirmative action and welfare of mathematicians
rubrics_metrics.description: (original phrasing) "These positions imply advocacy of affirmative action, concern for the welfare of individual mathematicians, concern over educational issues, and advocacy for research support for larger numbers of mathematicians."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support policies and programs that promote fair access, member well-being, and broader distribution of research funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote interdisciplinary work between mathematics and other sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: (original phrasing) "I am interested in the rich interplay between various branches of mathematics, physics and biology. I see such work as vital for the health of mathematics ..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage workshops, conferences, joint programs and funding mechanisms that foster productive cross-disciplinary collaborations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide meaningful aid to young mathematicians in hard times
rubrics_metrics.description: (original phrasing) "by providing meaningful aid to young mathematicians in hard times"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement support programs (fellowships, bridge funding, mentoring, career services) targeted at early-career researchers facing adverse job/funding conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence funding agencies and seek new funding sources
rubrics_metrics.description: (original phrasing) "by aggressively influencing funding agencies (and by coming up with new sources of money)"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active advocacy and fundraising to increase resources for mathematical research, including building relationships with agencies and exploring alternative funding models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use AMS publications and meetings to promote research and mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: (original phrasing) "Besides through its publications and meetings, [AMS] can realize these goals in a number of important ways..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage AMS journals, Notices, meetings, and summer institutes to advance research, education, and public engagement objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote diversity in nominations and AMS leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: (original phrasing) "I will recommend the best qualified mathematicians, with special care to promote the candidacies of women and minorities for AMS offices, council, committees, and boards ..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt nomination practices and selection criteria that actively encourage diverse candidates for leadership and committee roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support programs to retain students (freshman-level interventions)
rubrics_metrics.description: (original phrasing) "initiated a freshman program to hold students in mathematics (EXXON);"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend and fund freshman-level curricula and support programs designed to increase retention in mathematics majors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiate cooperative research and updating programs
rubrics_metrics.description: (original phrasing) "initiated cooperative research programs with minority institutions; initiated a program to bring college teachers into the University for updating (PEW, DANA);"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create and support collaborative programs that connect research institutions with minority-serving and teaching-focused institutions for capacity building and professional development.
